facts.why: The restaurant dinner is Miranda's birthday, not Stu's, and Stu is eating jambalaya, which is the dish Daniel seasons with cayenne.
facts.applied_note: Kept steak: the recipe is a sirloin, so jambalaya would not match the cook. The birthday is now Miranda's.

facts.text: Stu's birthday dinner, the night of the cayenne pepper
facts.why: It was Miranda's birthday dinner. Stu has a pepper allergy and Daniel sneaks cayenne into his jambalaya.
facts.fix: Miranda's birthday dinner, the night of the cayenne pepper

facts.text: Shepherd's pie she passes off as hers
facts.why: Daniel does learn to cook as Mrs Doubtfire, but no source shows a shepherd's pie or anything passed off as hers. The only home-cooked dinner shown is spaghetti and garlic bread.

facts.text: Hello, dears. Supper is on the table. Do not ask what is in the pot.
facts.why: Printed in quote marks as Mrs. Doubtfire's words, but it is not a line from the film. I could not open a quote page for this pass (the search tool was out of budget), so there is no quote source.
facts.fix: Hello, dears. Supper is on the table. Mind the frosting, and do not ask questions.

fix_note.text: Hello, dears. Supper is on the table. Mind the frosting, and do not ask questions.

facts.why: Only one dinner is a birthday, Miranda's. The other is Lundy's business dinner at the same restaurant and time.
facts.fix: Two dinners at once, one costume

vibe.verdict: A family kitchen placemat with the cake, the cayenne and the fruit drive-by, but it mixes up whose birthday it is and misses the nanny's best bits.
